MEMO

To: All Staff, Hawthorne Gas & Electric, Riverbend Office
From: Curtis Delgado, Facilities Manager
Date: July 14
Re: Building Energy Conservation Measures — August Trial

As an energy provider, we are often asked whether we follow the conservation advice we give customers. This August, the Riverbend office will pilot a set of internal conservation measures, and the results will be shared publicly in our autumn sustainability report.

The following changes will be in place from August 3 to August 31. Cooling setpoints will rise from 22 to 24 degrees Celsius in open work areas; conference rooms will remain at 22 degrees when booked. Lighting in corridors and storage areas will switch to occupancy sensors, which facilities crews will install during the last week of July, outside business hours. Window blinds on the south side of the building should be lowered by 11:00 A.M. each day — reminders will appear on the building's digital displays. Finally, the cafeteria will replace its two oldest refrigerated display cases, which together consume more electricity than all the office's printers combined.

We anticipate a reduction of roughly twelve percent in the building's August electricity use compared with last August. Staff who have concerns about workspace comfort — particularly those near the south windows — should contact the facilities help desk, and desk fans will be provided on request.

If the trial meets its target, the measures will be made permanent here and extended to our Lakeshore and Dunmore offices next year.

options: To comply with a new energy regulation
To demonstrate that the company follows its own advice and report results publicly
To reduce the cost of an upcoming renovation
To test products before selling them to customers

questions.question: What is suggested about the cafeteria's two oldest display cases?

Last year, orders submitted during the final week before the holidays were thirty percent larger on average than normal, and several products — particularly pediatric fever reducers and cold remedies — sold out at the wholesale level. Accounts that ordered early received full allocations, while later orders were partially filled.

For urgent patient-specific needs during the reduced-service period, our emergency line at 555-0186 will operate daily, including holidays, from 8:00 A.M. to 8:00 P.M. Emergency orders are limited to medically necessary items and ship by courier at no extra charge — a service we provide at cost because patient care comes first.

Finally, please verify your delivery address and receiving hours in the account portal by December 1, as holiday staffing changes at your location may affect delivery acceptance.

Nordica Pharmaceuticals Distribution Team

MEMO

To: All Loan Officers and Branch Managers, Pellworth Community Bank
From: Susannah Greer, Director of Community Lending
Date: March 24
Re: Launch of the Storefront Revival Loan Program

On April 14, Pellworth Community Bank will launch the Storefront Revival Loan, a new product supporting small businesses that renovate street-level commercial spaces in the Old Mill and Tannery Row districts. The program is funded in part by a development grant from the city, which allows us to offer rates 1.5 percentage points below our standard commercial renovation loans.

Key terms: loans range from $20,000 to $150,000, with repayment periods up to ten years. Eligible expenses include facade restoration, accessibility improvements, signage, and interior renovations of customer-facing areas. Back-office improvements and inventory purchases are not eligible under the grant's terms, so applications mixing eligible and ineligible costs must itemize them separately.

Applicants must hold a current business license, have operated for at least one year, and provide a contractor's estimate with their application. Because grant funds are capped, the program will accept applications only until allocated funds are exhausted — based on inquiry volume so far, we project this could occur within four months.

A briefing for loan officers will be held on April 2 at the main office, repeated by videoconference on April 4. Marketing materials, including window posters for participating branches, will arrive by April 9. Direct program questions to my office; media inquiries must go to corporate communications.

Higher fees charged at application

Dana Okafor (7:48 A.M.): Luis, are you at the warehouse yet? The cycle count for aisle 14 is due to the regional office by noon.
Luis Mendes (7:50 A.M.): Just clocked in. Grabbing a handheld scanner now. Bad news—two of our four scanners are still at the repair shop.
Dana Okafor (7:52 A.M.): Then take the one on my desk. The battery only lasts about three hours, so keep the charger with you.
Luis Mendes (7:55 A.M.): Will do. By the way, the system shows 240 cases of printer paper in aisle 14, but I only counted 212 on Friday.
Dana Okafor (7:57 A.M.): That gap again? Check whether the overflow racks in aisle 15 are holding the rest. Receiving sometimes shelves extra stock there without updating the location code.
Luis Mendes (8:06 A.M.): Good call. Found 26 cases on the overflow rack. Still two short, though.
Dana Okafor (8:08 A.M.): Two we can live with. Note it as shrinkage on the report, scan the overflow cases to the correct location, and send me the file before 11 so I can review it.
Luis Mendes (8:10 A.M.): On it. You'll have it by 10:30.

questions.question: Why does Ms. Okafor contact Mr. Mendes?

To confirm progress on an inventory count that has a deadline
To request that he reorder printer paper
To tell him the regional office is visiting

The receiving team sometimes shelves extra stock in aisle 15 without updating records.
Another branch borrowed the missing cases.

questions.question: At 8:08 A.M., what does Ms. Okafor most likely mean when she writes, "Two we can live with"?

A shortage of two cases is an acceptable discrepancy.
Two employees should finish the report together.
The count can be submitted two hours late.

Take the scanners to the repair shop
Recount the entire warehouse
Meet the regional office staff
questions.explanation: Ms. Okafor가 'send me the file before 11 so I can review it'이라고 요청하자 Mr. Mendes는 'You'll have it by 10:30'이라고 답했습니다. 즉 10시 30분까지 재고 조사 보고서 파일을 보낼 것임을 알 수 있습니다.

A copy of an insurance certificate
A payment for parking spaces
questions.explanation: 6:34 A.M. 메시지에서 'we owe him a copy of our insurance certificate before anyone loads in'이라고 했으므로, 장비 반입 전에 보험 증명서 사본을 건물 관리인에게 제출해야 합니다. Mr. Stone은 제작 사무실이 한 시간 내로 보내도록 하겠다고 답했습니다.

passage:
Jess Parker (5:32 P.M.): Heads-up: the lighting van won't start. I'm stuck at the rental house with all of Omar's fixtures.
Mei Lin (5:33 P.M.): How bad? We start prelighting the diner set at 7 tonight.
Jess Parker (5:35 P.M.): The garage thinks it's the alternator. Two hours minimum, and that's if the part is in stock.
Omar Haddad (5:36 P.M.): I can't prelight with nothing. Can we get a cargo van and transfer the gear?
Mei Lin (5:38 P.M.): Viktor, isn't your camera truck still half-empty? You loaded out early today.
Viktor Ruiz (5:40 P.M.): It is. I can be at the rental house in 25 minutes. The lighting cases should fit if we leave the dolly track behind.
Omar Haddad (5:41 P.M.): Track can wait—we won't lay any until tomorrow.
Mei Lin (5:43 P.M.): Then it's settled. Jess, stay with the van and text me the garage's invoice. Viktor, take Route 9; the bridge on Mill Street is closed.
Jess Parker (5:45 P.M.): Got it. I'll ride back with the repaired van tonight or first thing tomorrow.

questions.question: What problem does Ms. Parker report?
options: A van carrying lighting equipment will not start.
Some rented fixtures were damaged.
The diner set is not ready for filming.
A garage overcharged for a repair.
questions.explanation: 첫 메시지에서 'the lighting van won't start. I'm stuck at the rental house with all of Omar's fixtures'라고 하여, 조명 장비를 실은 밴이 시동이 걸리지 않아 대여 업체에 발이 묶였다는 것이 문제임을 알 수 있습니다.

questions.question: Why does Ms. Lin mention Mr. Ruiz's camera truck?
options: It needs to be returned to the rental house.
It has space available to carry the lighting gear.
It is blocking the entrance to the set.
It was recently repaired at the same garage.
questions.explanation: Mr. Haddad가 화물 밴을 구해 장비를 옮기자고 제안하자, Ms. Lin은 Viktor의 카메라 트럭이 아직 반쯤 비어 있지 않냐고 묻습니다. 이는 그 트럭의 남는 공간을 이용해 조명 장비를 운반하자는 의도입니다. 실제로 Viktor가 25분 안에 가서 싣겠다고 답합니다.

questions.question: At 5:41 P.M., what does Mr. Haddad most likely mean when he writes, "Track can wait"?
options: The dolly track is not needed until the following day.
A delivery is delayed on the railway.
He wants Viktor to drive more slowly.
The repair should be postponed for a week.
questions.explanation: Viktor가 돌리 트랙을 두고 가면 조명 케이스가 다 실릴 것이라고 하자, Mr. Haddad는 'Track can wait—we won't lay any until tomorrow'라고 답합니다. 즉 돌리 트랙은 내일까지 설치할 일이 없으므로 지금 당장 옮기지 않아도 된다는 의미입니다.

questions.question: What is Mr. Ruiz instructed to do?
options: Wait at the garage for an invoice
Pick up catering on the way to the set
Use Route 9 instead of Mill Street
Load the dolly track first
questions.explanation: Ms. Lin은 5:43 P.M. 메시지에서 'Viktor, take Route 9; the bridge on Mill Street is closed'라고 지시합니다. Mill Street의 다리가 폐쇄되었으므로 9번 도로로 우회하라는 지시입니다. 정비소 송장 문자는 Jess에게 한 지시입니다.

passage:
Andre Boyd (11:02 A.M.): Greta, the contractor can refinish the main court floor next week, but they need four consecutive days with zero foot traffic.
Greta Lindqvist (11:04 A.M.): The youth league plays Tuesday and Thursday evenings. Moving them is the problem.
Andre Boyd (11:06 A.M.): What about the auxiliary gym? The bleachers there only seat eighty, though.
Greta Lindqvist (11:08 A.M.): Attendance for weeknight games rarely tops sixty. I'll confirm with the league office, but I think we're fine.
Andre Boyd (11:10 A.M.): Then I'll tell the contractor Monday through Thursday. They'll sand Monday, seal Tuesday and Wednesday, and the floor needs all of Thursday to cure.
Greta Lindqvist (11:12 A.M.): Book it. Also ask whether the fumes will reach the fitness studio upstairs. We have prenatal classes there on Wednesday mornings.
Andre Boyd (11:14 A.M.): Good thinking. If they will, I'll move the class to the community room and bring in portable fans.
Greta Lindqvist (11:15 A.M.): And post notices at both entrances by Friday so members aren't surprised.

questions.question: What work is being scheduled at the facility?
options: Replacing the bleachers in the auxiliary gym
Refinishing the main court floor
Installing new ventilation upstairs
Expanding the fitness studio
questions.explanation: 첫 메시지에서 'the contractor can refinish the main court floor next week'라고 했으므로, 메인 코트 바닥 재마감 공사 일정을 잡는 것이 대화의 주제입니다. 공사 기간 동안 출입이 전면 금지되어야 한다는 조건 때문에 일정 조율이 필요해졌습니다.

questions.question: According to Mr. Boyd, what will happen on Thursday?
options: The floor will be sanded.
A second coat of sealant will be applied.
The floor will be left to cure.
The youth league will play on the main court.
questions.explanation: 11:10 A.M. 메시지에서 'They'll sand Monday, seal Tuesday and Wednesday, and the floor needs all of Thursday to cure'라고 일정이 제시됩니다. 월요일은 샌딩, 화·수요일은 실런트 도포, 목요일은 종일 건조(cure)에 쓰이므로 정답은 바닥 건조입니다.

questions.question: At 11:08 A.M., what does Ms. Lindqvist most likely mean when she writes, "I think we're fine"?
options: The contractor's price is within budget.
The auxiliary gym's seating should be sufficient for league games.
The league office has already approved the change.
The floor is in better condition than expected.
questions.explanation: Mr. Boyd가 보조 체육관의 관람석이 80석뿐이라고 우려하자, Ms. Lindqvist는 평일 저녁 경기 관중이 60명을 넘는 일이 드물다고 언급한 뒤 'I think we're fine'이라고 말합니다. 즉 80석이면 평소 관중을 수용하기에 충분할 것이라는 의미입니다. 리그 사무국 확인은 아직 하지 않았으므로 세 번째 선택지는 오답입니다.

questions.question: What will Mr. Boyd do if fumes are likely to reach the fitness studio?
options: Cancel the prenatal classes for the week
Postpone the refinishing work
Relocate a class to the community room
Ask the contractor to work at night
questions.explanation: Ms. Lindqvist가 위층 피트니스 스튜디오까지 냄새가 올라오는지 확인하라고 하자, Mr. Boyd는 'If they will, I'll move the class to the community room and bring in portable fans'라고 답했습니다. 즉 수업을 취소하는 것이 아니라 커뮤니티 룸으로 옮기고 이동식 환풍기를 들이겠다는 계획입니다.

passage:
Dev Patel (6:40 A.M.): The circulation pump for the lap pool tripped its breaker again overnight. Third time this month. Water clarity is already borderline.
Sam Torres (6:42 A.M.): Can it limp through the 7 A.M. swim club session?
Dev Patel (6:44 A.M.): I wouldn't risk it. If the motor seizes, we're closed for a week instead of a day.
Ingrid Walsh (6:45 A.M.): Then I'll cancel the morning session and shift club practice to the leisure pool tonight—the lanes are shorter, but it's better than nothing.
Sam Torres (6:47 A.M.): Agreed. Dev, what do we need for a permanent fix?
Dev Patel (6:50 A.M.): A new pump assembly. Aquatech quoted $3,900 last month, and they can install on Thursday if we order by noon today.
Sam Torres (6:52 A.M.): That's above my approval limit. I'll walk it up to the director right now and call you within the hour.
Ingrid Walsh (6:54 A.M.): While you do that, I'll post the closure on the app and put signs on the locker room doors.

questions.question: What problem is the team discussing?
options: A leak in the leisure pool
A repeatedly failing pool circulation pump
A shortage of swim instructors
A scheduling error in the club calendar
questions.explanation: Mr. Patel의 첫 메시지에서 랩 풀의 순환 펌프 차단기가 이번 달에만 세 번째로 내려갔고 수질도 한계 수준이라고 보고합니다. 반복적으로 고장 나는 순환 펌프가 대화의 핵심 문제입니다.

questions.question: At 6:44 A.M., what does Mr. Patel most likely mean when he writes, "I wouldn't risk it"?
options: Running the pump could lead to a much longer closure.
The swim club might cancel its membership.
The breaker is too dangerous to reset.
The repair quote may increase.
questions.explanation: Mr. Torres가 오전 7시 수영 클럽 시간까지 펌프를 그냥 돌릴 수 있는지 묻자, Mr. Patel은 'I wouldn't risk it. If the motor seizes, we're closed for a week instead of a day'라고 답합니다. 무리하게 가동했다가 모터가 완전히 망가지면 하루가 아니라 일주일을 폐장해야 하므로 위험을 감수하지 말자는 의미입니다.

questions.question: What does Ms. Walsh plan to do about the swim club's practice?
options: Cancel it for the entire week
Move it to another facility across town
Hold it in the leisure pool in the evening
Shorten it to thirty minutes
questions.explanation: 6:45 A.M. 메시지에서 Ms. Walsh는 아침 세션을 취소하고 클럽 연습을 오늘 밤 레저 풀로 옮기겠다('shift club practice to the leisure pool tonight')고 했습니다. 레인이 짧지만 아예 없는 것보다 낫다고 덧붙였습니다.

questions.question: Why will Mr. Torres speak with the director?
options: To report Mr. Patel's overtime hours
To get approval for a purchase that exceeds his spending limit
To complain about Aquatech's service
To request additional lifeguards
questions.explanation: 새 펌프 어셈블리 견적이 $3,900인데, Mr. Torres는 'That's above my approval limit. I'll walk it up to the director'라고 말합니다. 즉 자신의 결재 한도를 초과하는 금액이므로 디렉터의 승인을 받으러 가는 것입니다. 정오까지 주문해야 목요일 설치가 가능하다는 시간 제약도 이유가 됩니다.

passage:
Noor Karimi (1:15 P.M.): Felix, tomorrow's author talk just jumped from 60 registrations to 95. Can the Hartwell Room handle that?
Felix Grant (1:17 P.M.): Fire code caps it at 80 with rows of chairs. The Atrium holds 120, but the projector there has been flickering.
Noor Karimi (1:19 P.M.): The speaker's slides are mostly photographs, so a dying projector won't do. Any loaners?
Felix Grant (1:21 P.M.): The media lab has one we can borrow overnight. I'll test it on the Atrium screen before 5 today.
Noor Karimi (1:23 P.M.): Please do. Also, the author requested a lectern with a reading light and two bottles of still water—nothing sparkling.
Felix Grant (1:25 P.M.): Noted. The lectern light burned out last month, so I'll clip a fresh one on. What about the book table?
Noor Karimi (1:27 P.M.): Page & Vine Booksellers arrive at 5:30 to set up sales near the entrance. Leave them the folding tables by the coat check.
Felix Grant (1:29 P.M.): Done. I'll have the chairs, lectern, and projector checked off by the end of the day, and I'll prop the loading door open for the booksellers.

questions.question: Why is the event being moved out of the Hartwell Room?
options: The room's projector is broken.
Registrations now exceed the room's legal capacity.
The room is being painted.
The author requested a smaller space.
questions.explanation: 등록자가 60명에서 95명으로 늘었는데, Mr. Grant에 따르면 Hartwell Room은 소방 규정상 의자 배치 시 최대 80명까지만 수용할 수 있습니다('Fire code caps it at 80'). 따라서 정원 초과로 120명을 수용하는 Atrium으로 옮기는 것입니다. 프로젝터가 문제인 곳은 Atrium입니다.

questions.question: At 1:19 P.M., what does Ms. Karimi most likely mean when she writes, "a dying projector won't do"?
options: The talk should proceed without any slides.
A reliable projector is essential because the presentation depends on images.
The projector should be thrown away immediately.
The speaker prefers printed handouts.
questions.explanation: 연사의 슬라이드가 대부분 사진('mostly photographs')이라고 언급한 직후에 한 말이므로, 화면이 깜빡거리는 불안정한 프로젝터로는 행사를 치를 수 없고 제대로 작동하는 프로젝터가 반드시 필요하다는 뜻입니다. 그래서 바로 대여 가능한 기기가 있는지 묻고 있습니다.

questions.question: What did the author request?
options: A wireless microphone and sparkling water
A lectern with a reading light and still water
A table near the coat check
An overnight stay near the library
questions.explanation: 1:23 P.M. 메시지에서 작가는 독서등이 달린 연단(lectern with a reading light)과 탄산이 없는 생수 두 병('two bottles of still water—nothing sparkling')을 요청했다고 명시되어 있습니다.

questions.question: Who will arrive at 5:30 P.M.?
options: The author of the book
A bookseller setting up a sales table
A projector repair technician
Additional registration staff
questions.explanation: Ms. Karimi는 'Page & Vine Booksellers arrive at 5:30 to set up sales near the entrance'라고 했습니다. 즉 5시 30분에 도착하는 것은 입구 근처에 도서 판매대를 설치할 서점 직원들입니다. Mr. Grant는 이들을 위해 하역용 문을 열어 두겠다고 했습니다.

passage:
Adam Rossi (9:20 A.M.): Reminder—Saturday's reading festival setup starts at 8 A.M. We have four stations: the storytelling corner, craft tables, puppet stage, and the book swap.
Bella Fontaine (9:22 A.M.): I had nine volunteers confirmed, but two just dropped out—both were assigned to crafts.
Dana Phillips (9:24 A.M.): The teen advisory group owes service hours. I can ask two of them to cover crafts.
Bella Fontaine (9:25 A.M.): That solves it. Send me their names so I can add them to the sign-in sheet.
Chen Wei (9:27 A.M.): Quick flag: the puppet stage is stored in pieces, and the cart it sits on has a cracked wheel. Carrying everything up from the basement takes three people.
Adam Rossi (9:29 A.M.): Could we set it up Friday after closing instead?
Chen Wei (9:31 A.M.): Works for me. I'm here until 9 on Friday anyway.
Dana Phillips (9:33 A.M.): Approved—just keep the fire exits clear overnight. Adam, send the final floor plan to everyone by Thursday noon.
Adam Rossi (9:35 A.M.): Will do, and I'll bring extension cords for the glue guns at the craft tables.

questions.question: What problem does Ms. Fontaine mention?
options: The festival has too few registered children.
Two volunteers withdrew from the craft station.
The sign-in sheet was misplaced.
The storytelling corner has no chairs.
questions.explanation: 9:22 A.M. 메시지에서 Ms. Fontaine은 확정되었던 자원봉사자 9명 중 2명이 막 빠졌고, 둘 다 공예(crafts) 코너에 배정되어 있었다고 알립니다. 이것이 그녀가 제기한 문제입니다.

questions.question: How will the craft station most likely be staffed?
options: By members of the teen advisory group
By paid temporary workers
By Mr. Chen and Mr. Rossi
By parents of festival attendees
questions.explanation: Ms. Phillips가 봉사 시간이 필요한 청소년 자문 그룹(teen advisory group)의 두 명에게 공예 코너를 맡기겠다고 제안했고, Ms. Fontaine이 'That solves it'이라며 받아들였습니다. 따라서 공예 코너는 청소년 자문 그룹원들이 맡게 됩니다.

questions.question: At 9:31 A.M., what does Mr. Chen most likely mean when he writes, "I'm here until 9 on Friday anyway"?
options: He is unhappy about working late on Friday.
He can help assemble the puppet stage on Friday evening without changing his schedule.
He wants someone to cover his Friday shift.
The library will stay open later than usual on Friday.
questions.explanation: Mr. Rossi가 인형극 무대를 금요일 폐관 후에 미리 설치하자고 제안하자, Mr. Chen은 'Works for me'라고 동의하며 어차피 금요일에는 9시까지 근무한다고 덧붙입니다. 즉 자신의 기존 근무 일정상 금요일 저녁 설치 작업을 돕는 데 아무 지장이 없다는 의미입니다.

questions.question: What is Mr. Rossi asked to do by Thursday noon?
options: Repair a cart's cracked wheel
Purchase extension cords
Distribute the final floor plan
Collect the volunteers' service forms
questions.explanation: Ms. Phillips는 금요일 사전 설치를 승인하면서 'Adam, send the final floor plan to everyone by Thursday noon'이라고 지시했습니다. 따라서 목요일 정오까지 최종 배치도를 모두에게 보내는 것이 Mr. Rossi의 과제입니다. 연장 코드는 그가 자발적으로 가져오겠다고 한 것입니다.

passage:
Marco Diaz (9:05 A.M.): Lena, we're down to half a tank of propane and maybe 30 tortillas. Friday lunch at the courthouse plaza will blow through both.
Lena Vargas (9:07 A.M.): I thought the tortilla delivery came on Wednesdays?
Marco Diaz (9:09 A.M.): The supplier pushed it to Monday—their van is in the shop. I told you... actually no, that message is still sitting in my drafts. Sorry.
Lena Vargas (9:11 A.M.): That explains it. OK, I'll swing by Restaurant Depot for tortillas at 10. Can you handle the propane swap at the U-Gas on Fifth?
Marco Diaz (9:13 A.M.): Sure, but the truck has to be at the plaza by 10:45 to keep our spot. The lunch crowd starts lining up at 11:15.
Lena Vargas (9:15 A.M.): Then take the tank in my pickup instead of moving the truck. The keys are on the hook in the commissary.
Marco Diaz (9:17 A.M.): Smart. I'll drop the tank off, prep the salsa at the commissary, and meet you at the plaza by 10:30.
Lena Vargas (9:18 A.M.): Grab extra foil too. We ran out mid-service last Friday, and I'm not doing that again.

questions.question: What problem does Mr. Diaz report?
options: The food truck failed a city inspection.
Supplies are running low before a busy lunch service.
The courthouse plaza canceled their permit.
A competitor took their usual parking spot.
questions.explanation: 첫 메시지에서 프로판 가스가 반 통밖에 없고 토르티야도 약 30장뿐인데, 금요일 법원 광장 점심 장사로는 둘 다 바닥날 것이라고 보고합니다. 즉 바쁜 점심 영업을 앞두고 재료와 연료가 부족한 것이 문제입니다.

questions.question: What is suggested about Mr. Diaz?
options: He forgot to send a message about a delivery change.
He damaged the supplier's delivery van.
He usually shops at Restaurant Depot.
He recently started working for Ms. Vargas.
questions.explanation: Ms. Vargas가 토르티야 배달이 수요일 아니었냐고 묻자, Mr. Diaz는 공급업체가 월요일로 미뤘다고 알리려던 메시지가 'still sitting in my drafts', 즉 보내지 못한 채 임시 저장함에 남아 있었다며 사과합니다. 따라서 배달 변경 소식을 전달하는 것을 잊었음을 알 수 있습니다.

questions.question: Why does Ms. Vargas tell Mr. Diaz to use her pickup truck?
options: The food truck is too large for the gas station.
Her pickup gets better fuel mileage.
The food truck needs to stay free to reach the plaza on time.
The propane tank is already in her pickup.
questions.explanation: Mr. Diaz가 푸드트럭이 자리를 지키려면 10시 45분까지 광장에 도착해야 한다고 하자, Ms. Vargas는 트럭을 움직이지 말고 자신의 픽업트럭에 가스통을 실어 가라고 제안합니다. 즉 푸드트럭의 이동 시간을 아껴 제시간에 광장에 가도록 하기 위함입니다.

questions.question: At 9:18 A.M., what does Ms. Vargas most likely mean when she writes, "I'm not doing that again"?
options: She refuses to work at the courthouse plaza on Fridays.
She wants to avoid running out of foil during service again.
She will not lend her pickup truck in the future.
She plans to stop ordering from the current supplier.
questions.explanation: 바로 앞 문장에서 '지난 금요일 영업 도중에 포일이 다 떨어졌다(We ran out mid-service last Friday)'고 했으므로, 'I'm not doing that again'은 영업 중 포일이 바닥나는 상황을 다시는 겪지 않겠다는 뜻입니다. 그래서 여분의 포일을 챙기라고 지시한 것입니다.

passage:
Sal Romano (4:50 P.M.): Just checked in at the Riverfront Festival office. They moved us—Lot C, not the main promenade.
Becky Ahn (4:52 P.M.): What? We paid for a premium spot. Lot C is behind the parking structure; nobody walks through there.
Sal Romano (4:54 P.M.): The coordinator says our generator exceeds the promenade's new noise limit—anything over 65 decibels gets relocated.
Tasha Greene (4:55 P.M.): The quiet inverter generator is still at the shop after the carburetor work. We could pick it up before they close at 6.
Becky Ahn (4:57 P.M.): Do it. Sal, ask the coordinator in writing: if we run the quiet unit, do we get our promenade spot back?
Sal Romano (5:02 P.M.): She says yes—show the spec sheet at the gate tomorrow and we're back on the promenade.
Tasha Greene (5:04 P.M.): Heading to the shop now. Becky, the repair was $180; can you transfer that to my card?
Becky Ahn (5:06 P.M.): Sent. Print two copies of the spec sheet, Sal—one for the gate and one for our service window in case anyone asks.

questions.question: Why was the food truck assigned to a different location?
options: Its permit application was submitted late.
Its generator is louder than the new noise limit allows.
The main promenade is under construction.
Another vendor paid more for the spot.
questions.explanation: Mr. Romano가 4:54 P.M.에 전한 바에 따르면, 행사 코디네이터는 트럭의 발전기가 산책로의 새 소음 기준(65데시벨)을 초과하여 재배치되었다고 설명했습니다. 따라서 발전기 소음이 이전의 원인입니다.

questions.question: At 4:52 P.M., what does Ms. Ahn most likely mean when she writes, "nobody walks through there"?
options: Lot C is closed to pedestrians for safety reasons.
The new location would attract very few customers.
The festival map does not show Lot C.
Employees cannot reach the truck in Lot C.
questions.explanation: 프리미엄 자리 비용을 지불했는데 주차 건물 뒤편의 Lot C로 옮겨졌다는 소식에 대한 반응입니다. '아무도 그곳을 지나다니지 않는다'는 말은 유동 인구가 거의 없어 손님을 끌기 어려운, 장사에 불리한 위치라는 불만을 표현한 것입니다.

questions.question: What will Ms. Greene do before 6 P.M.?
options: Pick up a quieter generator from a repair shop
Meet the festival coordinator at the gate
Print copies of a specification sheet
Measure the noise level of the current generator
questions.explanation: Ms. Greene은 카뷰레터 수리를 마친 저소음 인버터 발전기가 아직 정비소에 있으며, 6시 영업 종료 전에 찾아올 수 있다고 했습니다. Ms. Ahn이 'Do it'이라고 승인하자 'Heading to the shop now'라며 바로 출발했습니다.

questions.question: What does Ms. Ahn ask Mr. Romano to do?
options: Pay $180 for a repair
Get written confirmation from the coordinator and print spec sheets
Move the truck to the promenade immediately
File a complaint with the festival office
questions.explanation: Ms. Ahn은 4:57 P.M.에 저소음 발전기를 쓰면 산책로 자리를 돌려받을 수 있는지 서면으로(in writing) 확인하라고 했고, 5:06 P.M.에는 사양서(spec sheet)를 두 부 인쇄하라고 지시했습니다. $180 수리비는 Ms. Greene에게 송금한 것입니다.

passage:
Iris Caldwell (3:10 P.M.): Diego, small crisis—the dance studio double-booked us on Thursday. A ballet class has the room until 8 P.M.
Diego Fuentes (3:12 P.M.): Thursday is our only full-cast run before tech week. We can't shrink it to two hours.
Iris Caldwell (3:14 P.M.): Options: the church hall on Brimley Street is free from 5, or we move the run to Friday at the theater itself.
Diego Fuentes (3:16 P.M.): On Friday the crew is hanging lights—actors would be dodging ladders all night.
Iris Caldwell (3:18 P.M.): The church hall it is, then. It's $60 for the evening, and we'd need to bring our own rehearsal cubes—they have nothing but folding chairs.
Diego Fuentes (3:20 P.M.): Fine. Can the cubes fit in your hatchback, or do we need Aaron's van?
Iris Caldwell (3:22 P.M.): Aaron's van, definitely. I'll also tape out the stage dimensions on their floor before everyone arrives—their hall is a meter narrower than our stage.
Diego Fuentes (3:24 P.M.): Perfect. Send the change to the cast tonight and ask for thumbs-up replies so we know everyone saw it.

questions.question: What problem does Ms. Caldwell report?
options: A rehearsal space was double-booked.
Several cast members are ill.
The theater's lights are not working.
A ballet class was canceled.
questions.explanation: 첫 메시지에서 댄스 스튜디오 측이 목요일에 이중 예약을 받아서 발레 수업이 오후 8시까지 그 공간을 쓰게 되었다고 알립니다. 즉 리허설 장소의 이중 예약이 문제입니다.

questions.question: At 3:16 P.M., what does Mr. Fuentes most likely mean when he writes, "actors would be dodging ladders all night"?
options: The cast needs more stage-combat training.
The theater would be unsuitable on Friday because of lighting work.
The crew should finish hanging lights before dark.
The actors have refused to rehearse on Friday.
questions.explanation: 금요일에 극장에서 리허설을 하자는 대안에 대해, 그날은 크루가 조명을 설치하는 날이라 배우들이 밤새 사다리를 피해 다녀야 할 것이라고 말합니다. 이는 조명 작업 때문에 금요일의 극장은 전체 리허설 장소로 부적합하다는 뜻으로, 결국 교회 강당이 선택됩니다.

questions.question: What is indicated about the church hall?
options: It is available at no charge.
It is wider than the theater's stage.
It provides only folding chairs.
It is booked until 8 P.M. on Thursday.
questions.explanation: 3:18 P.M. 메시지에서 교회 강당은 하룻저녁에 $60이고, 접이식 의자 외에는 아무것도 없어('they have nothing but folding chairs') 리허설 큐브를 직접 가져가야 한다고 했습니다. 또한 3:22 P.M.에 무대보다 1미터 더 좁다고 했으므로 두 번째 선택지도 오답입니다.

questions.question: What does Mr. Fuentes ask Ms. Caldwell to do?
options: Notify the cast and request confirmation replies
Rent a larger van for the equipment
Negotiate a lower rental fee
Reschedule tech week
questions.explanation: 마지막 메시지에서 Mr. Fuentes는 오늘 밤 출연진에게 변경 사항을 보내고, 모두가 확인했는지 알 수 있도록 엄지척(thumbs-up) 답장을 요청하라고 했습니다. 밴은 Aaron의 것을 쓰기로 이미 정했고 대여나 요금 협상은 언급되지 않았습니다.

passage:
Maya Singh (10:02 A.M.): Fittings for the Act II costumes run Wednesday 2–6 in the wardrobe loft. I need each principal actor for 20 minutes. The sign-up sheet is on the call board.
Theo Marsh (10:05 A.M.): I'm on a voiceover job until 4 that day. Are any evening slots possible?
Maya Singh (10:07 A.M.): I can stay until 7, but the loft loses good daylight after 6, and the color check for your military coat really needs natural light.
Ruth Ellison (10:09 A.M.): Could Theo come Thursday at noon instead? The loft is free then.
Maya Singh (10:11 A.M.): Thursday works—but only if the alterations from his last fitting are back from the tailor. Gwen, any word?
Gwen O'Leary (10:14 A.M.): The tailor promised everything by Wednesday at 5 P.M. I'm picking the order up on my way in Thursday morning.
Theo Marsh (10:15 A.M.): Thursday noon it is. I'll skip lunch with the radio people.
Ruth Ellison (10:17 A.M.): Logged. Everyone else, grab a Wednesday slot by tomorrow, or I'll assign one to you myself.

questions.question: Why does Ms. Singh prefer to see Mr. Marsh before 6 P.M.?
options: The wardrobe loft closes at 6.
Checking a costume's color requires natural light.
The tailor leaves at 6.
Mr. Marsh's voiceover job starts in the evening.
questions.explanation: Ms. Singh은 7시까지 남을 수는 있지만 의상실 다락이 6시 이후에는 좋은 자연광을 잃고, Mr. Marsh의 군용 코트 색상 확인에는 자연광이 꼭 필요하다('the color check ... really needs natural light')고 설명합니다.

questions.question: What will Ms. O'Leary do on Thursday morning?
options: Post a sign-up sheet on the call board
Collect altered costumes from the tailor
Drive Mr. Marsh to his fitting
Set up lights in the wardrobe loft
questions.explanation: Ms. Singh이 지난 가봉 때 맡긴 수선품이 재단사에게서 돌아와야만 목요일 가봉이 가능하다고 하자, Ms. O'Leary는 재단사가 수요일 5시까지 끝내기로 했고 자신이 목요일 아침 출근길에 찾아오겠다('I'm picking the order up on my way in Thursday morning')고 답했습니다.

questions.question: What is suggested about Mr. Marsh?
options: He will give up a lunch appointment to attend his fitting.
He has never had a costume fitting before.
He works at the theater only on weekends.
He asked for a different costume design.
questions.explanation: 목요일 정오 가봉이 확정되자 Mr. Marsh는 'I'll skip lunch with the radio people', 즉 라디오(성우 작업) 관계자들과의 점심 약속을 건너뛰겠다고 말합니다. 가봉에 참석하기 위해 점심 약속을 포기하는 것입니다.

questions.question: At 10:17 A.M., what does Ms. Ellison most likely mean when she writes, "or I'll assign one to you myself"?
options: She will hire additional actors if needed.
Cast members who do not choose a time slot will be given one without their input.
She plans to attend every fitting personally.
She will take over the costume designer's duties.
questions.explanation: '내일까지 수요일 시간대를 직접 고르지 않으면 내가 직접 정해 주겠다'는 말로, 출연진이 스스로 가봉 시간을 신청하지 않을 경우 본인 의사와 상관없이 시간이 배정될 것이라는 일종의 경고이자 독려입니다. 빨리 신청하라는 의도가 담겨 있습니다.

passage:
Jamal Reed (2:12 P.M.): Karen, the city council just moved the budget vote up to 4 P.M. today. My harbor cleanup feature isn't done—which one do you want for the 6 o'clock?
Karen Doyle (2:14 P.M.): The vote, no question. The harbor piece can hold until the weekend edition.
Jamal Reed (2:16 P.M.): Then I need a camera operator. Sofia is filming the school board across town until 3:30.
Karen Doyle (2:18 P.M.): City hall is ten minutes from the school. I'll have her go straight there—you two can meet in the press room at 3:45.
Jamal Reed (2:20 P.M.): Cutting it close, but workable. Can graphics pull last year's budget numbers for a comparison chart?
Karen Doyle (2:22 P.M.): Already asked. Send your script by 5:15; the show is tight tonight, so you've got 90 seconds, not the usual two minutes.
Jamal Reed (2:24 P.M.): Ninety seconds for a $40 million story? You drive a hard bargain. I'll make it work.
Karen Doyle (2:26 P.M.): That's the spirit. If the vote runs late, call me—we'll go live from the chamber steps instead of running a packaged story.

questions.question: Why does Mr. Reed contact Ms. Doyle?
options: To request time off this weekend
To ask which story to prioritize after a schedule change
To report that his camera equipment is missing
To complain about the graphics department
questions.explanation: 시의회가 예산 표결을 오늘 오후 4시로 앞당기면서 진행 중이던 항만 정화 기획 기사와 일정이 겹치게 되자, Mr. Reed는 6시 뉴스에 어떤 기사를 내보낼지 편집장에게 묻고 있습니다. Ms. Doyle은 표결 기사를 우선하라고 답합니다.

questions.question: What will Sofia most likely do at around 3:30 P.M.?
options: Return to the newsroom to edit footage
Head directly from the school board meeting to city hall
Begin filming the harbor cleanup
Meet the graphics team about a chart
questions.explanation: Sofia는 3시 30분까지 교육위원회를 촬영 중인데, Ms. Doyle이 시청은 학교에서 10분 거리이니 곧장 시청으로 가게 하겠다('I'll have her go straight there')고 했습니다. 3시 45분에 기자실에서 Mr. Reed와 만나기로 했으므로, 촬영이 끝나는 대로 시청으로 이동할 것입니다.

questions.question: At 2:24 P.M., what does Mr. Reed most likely mean when he writes, "You drive a hard bargain"?
options: He thinks the time limit is demanding but he will accept it.
He wants to renegotiate his salary.
He believes the budget vote will fail.
He refuses to shorten his report.
questions.explanation: 4천만 달러짜리 기사를 평소의 2분이 아닌 90초에 다뤄야 한다는 지시에 대해 '참 야박한 조건을 내거시네요'라는 뉘앙스로 받아친 표현입니다. 곧바로 'I'll make it work'라고 했으므로, 조건이 빡빡하다고 느끼면서도 받아들이겠다는 의미입니다.

questions.question: According to Ms. Doyle, what will happen if the vote runs late?
options: The story will be dropped from the broadcast.
The station will air a live report from outside the council chamber.
The weekend edition will cover the vote instead.
The show will be extended by two minutes.
questions.explanation: 마지막 메시지에서 Ms. Doyle은 표결이 늦어지면 전화하라며, 편집된 녹화 기사 대신 의회 건물 계단에서 생방송으로 진행하겠다('we'll go live from the chamber steps')고 말합니다.

passage:
Owen Brooks (5:05 A.M.): Morning, team. Rundown change: the ferry strike talks collapsed overnight, so that's now our lead story.
Lucia Marini (5:07 A.M.): I saw the wire. Do we have anyone at the terminal for a live shot?
Owen Brooks (5:09 A.M.): Dispatching the overnight crew now; they should have a signal by 5:50. If not, we lead with the file footage and your voiceover.
Hank Forester (5:11 A.M.): Heads-up—fog is thick along the coast road. If the crew takes it, they'll never make 5:50. Send them by the highway.
Owen Brooks (5:12 A.M.): Good catch. Texting the driver now.
Lucia Marini (5:14 A.M.): Also, my teleprompter froze twice during yesterday's rehearsal. Can engineering look at it before air?
Owen Brooks (5:16 A.M.): They swapped the unit at midnight; you have the backup machine today. Scripts will load by 5:40.
Hank Forester (5:18 A.M.): One more thing—my fog graphics need 40 seconds, not 30. Cut me down somewhere else if you have to.
Owen Brooks (5:20 A.M.): Take 10 from your noon outlook. Everyone on set by 5:45, please.

questions.question: Why has the morning rundown changed?
options: A reporter called in sick.
Negotiations to end a ferry strike broke down overnight.
The teleprompter stopped working.
Heavy fog closed the studio.
questions.explanation: 첫 메시지에서 'the ferry strike talks collapsed overnight, so that's now our lead story'라고 했습니다. 페리 파업 협상이 밤사이 결렬되어 그 소식이 톱뉴스로 바뀌면서 방송 순서(rundown)가 변경된 것입니다.

questions.question: At 5:11 A.M., what does Mr. Forester most likely mean when he writes, "they'll never make 5:50"?
options: The crew will not arrive in time if they drive along the coast.
The broadcast should be delayed until 5:50.
The fog will not clear before the show ends.
The crew's camera cannot transmit a signal in fog.
questions.explanation: 해안 도로에 안개가 짙다고 알린 직후의 발언이므로, 중계팀이 해안 도로로 가면 5시 50분까지 신호를 잡아야 하는 시간 안에 도착할 수 없다는 뜻입니다. 그래서 고속도로로 보내라고 권했고, Mr. Brooks가 즉시 운전기사에게 문자를 보냈습니다.

questions.question: What is indicated about the teleprompter Ms. Marini will use?
options: It froze twice during yesterday's broadcast.
It is a backup unit installed overnight.
It will not be ready until 6 A.M.
It is being repaired by an outside vendor.
questions.explanation: Ms. Marini가 리허설 중 두 번 멈춘 텔레프롬프터의 점검을 요청하자, Mr. Brooks는 엔지니어링팀이 자정에 본체를 교체해서 오늘은 예비 장비(backup machine)를 쓰게 된다고 답했습니다. 멈춘 것은 어제 리허설 때이지 방송 중이 아니었습니다.

questions.question: How will Mr. Forester get extra time for his fog graphics?
options: The lead story will be shortened.
Ten seconds will be cut from his noon outlook segment.
The show will start five minutes early.
A commercial break will be dropped.
questions.explanation: 안개 그래픽 설명에 30초가 아닌 40초가 필요하다는 요청에 대해, Mr. Brooks는 'Take 10 from your noon outlook', 즉 그의 정오 전망 코너에서 10초를 줄여 충당하라고 지시했습니다.

passage:
Joel Kim (12:36 P.M.): Heidi, I'm at the Fairmont Hotel job, but the loading dock is blocked by a linen truck. The forecast says 34 degrees by 2—these hydrangeas won't like sitting in the van.
Heidi Brandt (12:38 P.M.): Did you call the landscaping foreman? He arranged a dock window for us from noon to 1.
Joel Kim (12:40 P.M.): Twice. It goes to voicemail. The hotel's security desk says the linen truck should clear out in about 20 minutes.
Heidi Brandt (12:42 P.M.): Twenty we can survive. Crack the van's roof vents and pull into the shade on the north side. Don't run the engine for the AC the whole time—you'll need that fuel for the Westbrook run.
Joel Kim (12:44 P.M.): Done. By the way, about the Westbrook order—I count 18 boxwoods on my manifest, but the invoice taped to the cart said 24.
Heidi Brandt (12:47 P.M.): The other six are still in quarantine after the leaf-spot scare. I'll ring Westbrook and tell them the rest will follow next week. Deliver the 18 with the revised invoice in the gray folder.
Joel Kim (12:49 P.M.): Found it. The dock's clearing now—going in.

questions.question: What problem does Mr. Kim report?
options: His delivery van has broken down.
He cannot unload because the loading dock is blocked.
The hotel canceled its plant order.
He left an invoice at the nursery.
questions.explanation: 첫 메시지에서 Fairmont Hotel의 하역장이 리넨 트럭에 막혀 있어 짐을 내릴 수 없고, 기온이 오르면 밴 안의 수국이 상할 수 있다고 보고합니다. 하역장 접근 불가가 핵심 문제입니다.

questions.question: At 12:42 P.M., what does Ms. Brandt most likely mean when she writes, "Twenty we can survive"?
options: A 20-minute wait should not seriously harm the plants.
Twenty hydrangeas can be left at the hotel.
The delivery is 20 minutes ahead of schedule.
The company can afford a $20 parking fee.
questions.explanation: 경비 데스크가 리넨 트럭이 약 20분 뒤에 빠질 것이라고 했다는 보고에 대한 답변입니다. 더위에 약한 수국이 걱정이지만 20분 정도의 대기는 버틸 수 있다는 뜻이며, 그동안 환기구를 열고 그늘에 차를 대라는 구체적인 지시가 이어집니다.

questions.question: Why does the manifest show fewer boxwoods than the original invoice?
options: Six were sold to another customer.
Six are being held in quarantine because of a plant disease concern.
Six were damaged during loading.
The customer reduced the order size.
questions.explanation: Ms. Brandt는 'The other six are still in quarantine after the leaf-spot scare'라고 설명합니다. 잎반점병 우려로 6그루가 격리 중이어서 적하 목록에는 18그루만 있는 것이며, 나머지는 다음 주에 보낼 예정입니다.

questions.question: What will Ms. Brandt most likely do next?
options: Call Westbrook about a partial delivery
Drive to the Fairmont Hotel
Print a new manifest for Mr. Kim
Contact the linen company
questions.explanation: 12:47 P.M. 메시지에서 'I'll ring Westbrook and tell them the rest will follow next week'라고 했으므로, Westbrook 고객에게 전화해 이번에는 18그루만 배송되고 나머지는 다음 주에 간다는 사실을 알릴 것입니다.

passage:
Greg Holt (8:15 A.M.): Big one, folks: Carrick Builders wants 120 junipers, 60 red maples, and 200 flats of groundcover for the Ashford Park project—delivered within three weeks.
Yuki Tanaka (8:18 A.M.): Junipers and groundcover, no problem. The maples are the issue: we have 35 at planting size. The rest would have to come from the Linden Valley growers.
Greg Holt (8:20 A.M.): Is their stock any good? Carrick rejected an entire shipment from us two years ago, remember.
Yuki Tanaka (8:22 A.M.): That was a different supplier. Linden Valley's trees passed our inspection in April. Still, I'd drive up and tag each maple myself.
Bree Connors (8:24 A.M.): If Yuki tags on Monday, I can schedule their freight for the second week and our own trucks for week three. Two deliveries, though—Carrick has to accept a split.
Greg Holt (8:26 A.M.): They'll take a split if the groundcover lands first; the planting crews start with the beds anyway. I'll write it into the contract.
Yuki Tanaka (8:28 A.M.): Booking the Linden Valley visit now. Send me the spec sheet so I tag to Carrick's standard, not ours.
Greg Holt (8:30 A.M.): On its way.

questions.question: What is the main difficulty with the Carrick Builders order?
options: The nursery does not have enough red maples in stock.
The delivery deadline has already passed.
The junipers failed an inspection.
The groundcover is out of season.
questions.explanation: Ms. Tanaka에 따르면 향나무와 지피식물은 문제없지만, 단풍나무는 식재 가능한 크기가 35그루뿐이라 60그루 주문을 채우려면 외부 재배자(Linden Valley)의 물량이 필요합니다. 재고 부족이 핵심 문제입니다.

questions.question: At 8:22 A.M., what does Ms. Tanaka most likely mean when she writes, "That was a different supplier"?
options: The past rejection should not raise doubts about Linden Valley's trees.
Carrick Builders has changed its purchasing team.
The nursery no longer works with outside growers.
Linden Valley caused the problem two years ago.
questions.explanation: Carrick이 2년 전 출하분 전체를 반품했던 일을 Mr. Holt가 우려하자, Ms. Tanaka는 그때는 다른 공급자였다고 답합니다. 즉 과거의 반품 사건은 Linden Valley와 무관하므로 그들의 품질을 의심할 근거가 되지 않는다는 의미이며, 4월 검사 통과 사실을 덧붙여 신뢰를 뒷받침합니다.

questions.question: What does Ms. Connors propose?
options: Renting additional delivery trucks
Splitting the order into two separate deliveries
Delaying the project by one month
Canceling the freight contract
questions.explanation: Ms. Connors는 Yuki가 월요일에 나무에 태그를 달면 둘째 주에 Linden Valley의 화물 운송을, 셋째 주에 자사 트럭 배송을 잡을 수 있다며, 두 번에 나누어 배송하는 방안(a split)을 Carrick이 받아들여야 한다고 제안합니다.

questions.question: Why does Ms. Tanaka ask for a spec sheet?
options: So she can calculate the shipping cost
So she can select trees according to the customer's standard
So she can order new tagging equipment
So she can update the nursery's catalog
questions.explanation: 마지막 부분에서 Ms. Tanaka는 'Send me the spec sheet so I tag to Carrick's standard, not ours'라고 요청합니다. 자사 기준이 아닌 고객사 Carrick의 규격 기준에 맞춰 단풍나무를 선별·태깅하기 위해 사양서가 필요한 것입니다.

passage:
Stefan Novak (10:22 A.M.): Alma, the front desk just called—the guest booked into the Garnet Suite is landing early and wants to check in at noon instead of 3.
Alma Reyes (10:24 A.M.): That suite checked out at 9, and it's a deep-clean day: carpets, drapes, the works. That's normally a four-hour turnaround.
Stefan Novak (10:26 A.M.): Can we pull the team from the eighth floor? Those rooms aren't due until 4.
Alma Reyes (10:28 A.M.): Take Dora and Felix, but the eighth floor still needs someone—a tour group arrives at 4 sharp. Leave Marisol there.
Stefan Novak (10:30 A.M.): Done. The carpet machine is acting up, though—it left streaks in 612 yesterday.
Alma Reyes (10:32 A.M.): Then skip the shampoo and spot-clean by hand. The guest's profile flags a fragrance allergy anyway—use the unscented line only, and that includes the laundry sheets.
Stefan Novak (10:34 A.M.): Noted. Fresh flowers from the lobby florist as usual?
Alma Reyes (10:36 A.M.): Yes, but tell Henri nothing heavily perfumed—no lilies. I'll inspect the suite myself at 11:45.

questions.question: Why does Mr. Novak contact Ms. Reyes?
options: A guest will be arriving three hours earlier than scheduled.
A suite was damaged during a deep cleaning.
A tour group canceled its reservation.
The lobby florist made a delivery error.
questions.explanation: 첫 메시지에서 Garnet Suite를 예약한 손님이 일찍 도착해 오후 3시 대신 정오에 체크인하기를 원한다고 전합니다. 평소 4시간이 걸리는 특별 청소일이라 일정이 빠듯해진 것이 대화의 발단입니다.

questions.question: At 10:24 A.M., what does Ms. Reyes most likely mean when she writes, "carpets, drapes, the works"?
options: The suite's carpets and drapes were recently replaced.
The suite requires a complete, thorough cleaning today.
The suite is being used to store equipment.
The carpets and drapes have been sent out for repair.
questions.explanation: 'the works'는 '전부, 모든 것'을 뜻하는 구어 표현입니다. 이날이 deep-clean day여서 카펫과 커튼을 포함해 모든 항목을 빠짐없이 청소해야 한다는 의미이며, 그래서 평소 4시간짜리 작업이라고 덧붙인 것입니다.

questions.question: Why must the staff use unscented products in the suite?
options: The hotel is switching to a new supplier.
Scented products damaged the carpet in another room.
The arriving guest has a fragrance allergy.
The general manager banned scented cleaners.
questions.explanation: 10:32 A.M. 메시지에서 'The guest's profile flags a fragrance allergy'라고 했습니다. 투숙객 프로필에 향료 알레르기가 표시되어 있으므로 세탁 시트까지 포함해 무향 제품만 사용해야 하며, 꽃도 향이 강한 백합은 피하라고 지시합니다.

questions.question: What will Ms. Reyes do at 11:45 A.M.?
options: Greet the guest in the lobby
Personally inspect the suite
Repair the carpet machine
Train the eighth-floor staff
questions.explanation: 마지막 메시지에서 'I'll inspect the suite myself at 11:45'라고 했으므로, 손님이 정오에 도착하기 전에 Ms. Reyes가 직접 스위트룸의 청소 상태를 점검할 것입니다.

passage:
Nadia Osman (1:40 P.M.): Team, we're 60 king sheet sets short for tonight's turnover. The laundry chute jam this morning put everything behind.
Leo Brennan (1:42 P.M.): The washers are running nonstop, but pressing is the bottleneck. Realistically, I can hand over 30 sets by 4 and the rest by 7.
Fatima Aziz (1:44 P.M.): My floor has 22 king rooms due before 5. The airline crew block starts arriving at 4:30.
Nadia Osman (1:46 P.M.): Crew rooms first, then. Leo, send Fatima's floor the first cart straight from pressing—skip the linen room.
Roy Jensen (1:48 P.M.): The Marlowe across the street owes us a favor from convention week. Want me to ask if they can lend us 30 sets?
Nadia Osman (1:50 P.M.): Make the call. Even 20 would take the pressure off.
Roy Jensen (1:58 P.M.): Their housekeeping manager says yes—25 sets, ready at their service entrance at 3. I'll take the van.
Nadia Osman (2:00 P.M.): Excellent. Log them as borrowed so they go back washed and pressed by Friday. Fatima, flag any room we can't finish by 5, and I'll have the front desk hold those assignments.

questions.question: What caused the linen shortage?
options: A supplier failed to make a delivery.
A laundry chute jam delayed the morning's washing.
Several washers broke down overnight.
An unusually large tour group checked in.
questions.explanation: 첫 메시지에서 'The laundry chute jam this morning put everything behind'라고 했습니다. 아침에 세탁물 투입구가 막히는 바람에 세탁 일정 전체가 지연되어 킹사이즈 시트 60세트가 부족해진 것입니다.

questions.question: Why are the rooms on Ms. Aziz's floor being prioritized?
options: They are the hotel's most expensive suites.
Airline crew members begin arriving at 4:30.
They were skipped during yesterday's cleaning.
A health inspection is scheduled there.
questions.explanation: Ms. Aziz가 자신의 층에 5시 전까지 준비해야 할 킹룸이 22개 있고 항공사 승무원 단체가 4시 30분부터 도착한다고 하자, Ms. Osman이 'Crew rooms first'라며 그 층에 다림질이 끝난 첫 카트를 바로 보내라고 지시합니다.

questions.question: At 1:50 P.M., what does Ms. Osman most likely mean when she writes, "Even 20 would take the pressure off"?
options: Even a partial loan of linens would ease the situation.
Twenty staff members should be reassigned.
The hotel should buy 20 new sheet sets.
Twenty rooms can be left uncleaned tonight.
questions.explanation: Mr. Jensen이 길 건너 Marlowe 호텔에서 30세트를 빌릴 수 있는지 알아보겠다고 하자 한 말입니다. 30세트가 아니라 20세트만 빌려도 부족분의 부담이 크게 줄어든다는 뜻으로, 빌릴 수 있는 만큼이라도 도움이 된다는 의미입니다. 실제로는 25세트를 빌리게 됩니다.

questions.question: What must happen by Friday?
options: The borrowed linens must be returned washed and pressed.
The laundry chute must be replaced.
The airline crew must check out.
A new linen supplier must be selected.
questions.explanation: 2:00 P.M. 메시지에서 Ms. Osman은 빌린 시트들을 대여품으로 기록해 두고 금요일까지 세탁과 다림질을 마쳐 돌려보내야 한다('they go back washed and pressed by Friday')고 지시했습니다.

passage:
Gus Antonelli (11:50 A.M.): Holly, the distributor just e-mailed. Only 80 copies of Salt Meridian arrive today—the other 70 are backordered until next Tuesday.
Holly Werner (11:52 A.M.): The signing is tomorrow at 6, and presales alone are 64. Walk-ins will wipe out the rest in minutes.
Gus Antonelli (11:54 A.M.): Could we cap sales at one copy per customer at the door?
Holly Werner (11:56 A.M.): Do that, and also call Inkwell Books in Marbury—they stocked the title for an event that got canceled. They might part with their copies.
Gus Antonelli (12:14 P.M.): Inkwell can spare 40 at cost if we pick them up today. Their owner asks that we mention their store at the event in return.
Holly Werner (12:16 P.M.): Small price. I'll thank them from the podium myself. Take the store card and a hatchback's worth of crates.
Gus Antonelli (12:18 P.M.): Leaving at 1. Should we offer signed bookplates to anyone who still misses out?
Holly Werner (12:20 P.M.): Yes—print vouchers tonight. The author already agreed to sign 100 bookplates before she leaves town on Thursday.

questions.question: What problem are the writers discussing?
options: An author canceled a signing event.
A book shipment is smaller than expected before an event.
A store's card reader is not working.
Presale customers requested refunds.
questions.explanation: 유통사에서 Salt Meridian이 오늘 80부만 도착하고 나머지 70부는 다음 주 화요일까지 입고가 지연된다고 알려 왔는데, 사인회는 내일이고 사전 판매분만 64부라 재고가 크게 부족한 상황입니다.

questions.question: What is suggested about Inkwell Books?
options: It is the closest branch of the same bookstore chain.
It has unsold copies because one of its events was canceled.
It ordered too few copies of the book.
It is hosting the author next week.
questions.explanation: Ms. Werner는 Marbury에 있는 Inkwell Books가 취소된 행사를 위해 이 책을 들여놓았다('they stocked the title for an event that got canceled')며, 그 재고를 넘겨줄 수도 있다고 말합니다. 실제로 40부를 원가에 제공하기로 합니다.

questions.question: At 12:16 P.M., what does Ms. Werner most likely mean when she writes, "Small price"?
options: The books from Inkwell are heavily discounted.
Mentioning the other store at the event is an easy condition to accept.
The signing tickets should cost less.
The delivery fee is lower than expected.
questions.explanation: Inkwell의 주인이 책 40부를 넘기는 대가로 행사에서 자기 서점을 언급해 달라고 요청했다는 말에 대한 반응입니다. 'Small price'는 그 정도 조건은 치르기에 아주 가벼운 대가라는 뜻이며, 직접 연단에서 감사 인사를 하겠다고 덧붙입니다.

questions.question: What will customers who cannot buy a book at the event receive?
options: A full refund and a gift card
A voucher for a signed bookplate
Free shipping on a future order
A ticket to the author's next event
questions.explanation: Mr. Antonelli의 제안에 따라, 행사장에서 책을 사지 못한 손님에게는 서명된 북플레이트 교환권(voucher)을 제공하기로 했습니다. 작가가 목요일에 떠나기 전 북플레이트 100장에 서명하기로 이미 동의한 상태입니다.

passage:
June Park (3:30 P.M.): Two hours to doors. The stanchions are up from the register to the cookbook aisle—that holds about 90 people.
Mark Jablonski (3:32 P.M.): Presale ticket holders should skip that line, though. Where do they wait?
June Park (3:34 P.M.): Reserved seating, rows one through four. Tessa is taping name cards now... actually, Tessa, are the wristbands here yet?
Tessa Moreau (3:36 P.M.): The courier dropped them off 10 minutes ago—gold for presale, blue for general admission. I'll band people at the door as they show their receipts.
Mark Jablonski (3:38 P.M.): Good. The author's flight landed at 2:50, so she'll be here around 4:30, and she wants 30 quiet minutes in the office before going on.
June Park (3:40 P.M.): I'll take coffee and the green-room snacks up there now. Should we move the poetry table? It pinches the line right at the corner.
Mark Jablonski (3:42 P.M.): Roll it into the stockroom—the last thing we need is a bottleneck on the local news. Channel 9 confirmed they're sending a camera.
Tessa Moreau (3:44 P.M.): Then I'll steam the banner, too. It's been folded in a box for a month.

questions.question: What event is the store preparing for?
options: A cookbook cooking demonstration
An author appearance with ticketed seating
A grand reopening sale
A poetry reading contest
questions.explanation: 사전 판매 티켓 소지자, 예약 좌석, 작가의 도착 시간과 대기실 준비, 손목 밴드 배부 등의 내용으로 보아 작가 사인회/출연 행사를 준비하고 있음을 알 수 있습니다. 요리책 코너와 시집 테이블은 단지 매장 내 위치로 언급될 뿐입니다.

questions.question: What is the purpose of the two wristband colors?
options: To distinguish presale buyers from general admission
To indicate which staff members are on duty
To show which customers want signed copies
To separate adults from children
questions.explanation: Ms. Moreau는 'gold for presale, blue for general admission'이라고 설명합니다. 금색은 사전 구매자, 파란색은 일반 입장객을 구분하기 위한 것으로, 영수증 확인 후 문에서 손목 밴드를 채워 줄 예정입니다.

questions.question: What will the author most likely do when she arrives?
options: Begin signing books immediately
Spend half an hour resting in the office
Give an interview to Channel 9
Inspect the reserved seating area
questions.explanation: Mr. Jablonski에 따르면 작가는 4시 30분쯤 도착해 무대에 오르기 전 사무실에서 조용한 30분('30 quiet minutes in the office before going on')을 원한다고 했습니다. 그래서 Ms. Park가 커피와 간식을 미리 가져다 두기로 합니다.

questions.question: At 3:42 P.M., what does Mr. Jablonski most likely mean when he writes, "the last thing we need is a bottleneck on the local news"?
options: He hopes the news report will be brief.
He wants to avoid a crowded line being shown on television.
He thinks the news crew should park elsewhere.
He expects few people to watch the broadcast.
questions.explanation: 시집 테이블이 모퉁이에서 줄을 좁힌다는 말에, 테이블을 창고로 치우라며 한 말입니다. Channel 9 카메라가 오기로 확정된 상황에서 줄이 막혀 혼잡한 모습이 지역 뉴스에 나오는 것만은 피하고 싶다는 의미입니다.

passage:
Ben Whitfield (1:05 P.M.): Vera, I found a full pallet in bay 31 labeled as ceramic tile, but it's shrink-wrapped boxes of faucets. The SKU on the boxes is FA-2210.
Vera Kovacs (1:07 P.M.): FA-2210... the system says we have zero of those and 14 backorders. Customers have been waiting three weeks.
Ben Whitfield (1:09 P.M.): So someone slapped the wrong pallet tag on it at receiving?
Vera Kovacs (1:11 P.M.): Looks like it. The tile shipment and the faucet shipment landed on the same day in May—both from Hargrove Imports. Easy mix-up.
Ben Whitfield (1:13 P.M.): Want me to retag it and move it to plumbing, row 6?
Vera Kovacs (1:15 P.M.): Hold off. If the faucets were never booked in, scanning them now will throw an error. Let me create a correction record first—give me 15 minutes.
Ben Whitfield (1:17 P.M.): Standing by. Should I check whether the actual tile pallet is hiding somewhere, too?
Vera Kovacs (1:19 P.M.): Please. Try bays 28 through 34 and the returns cage—receiving parks overflow there when the bays are full. If both records get fixed today, those 14 faucet orders ship tonight.

questions.question: What did Mr. Whitfield discover?
options: A pallet whose label does not match its contents
A shipment of damaged ceramic tile
An unlocked returns cage
A missing forklift in bay 31
questions.explanation: 첫 메시지에서 31번 베이의 팔레트가 세라믹 타일로 표기되어 있지만 실제 내용물은 수도꼭지(faucets) 상자라고 보고합니다. 즉 라벨과 내용물이 일치하지 않는 팔레트를 발견한 것입니다.

questions.question: What is indicated about SKU FA-2210?
options: It was discontinued in May.
Fourteen customer orders for it are waiting to be filled.
It is stored in the returns cage.
It was shipped to the wrong warehouse.
questions.explanation: Ms. Kovacs는 시스템상 FA-2210의 재고가 0인데 이월 주문(backorders)이 14건 있으며 고객들이 3주째 기다리고 있다고 말합니다. 따라서 처리 대기 중인 고객 주문이 14건이라는 것이 정답입니다.

questions.question: At 1:15 P.M., what does Ms. Kovacs most likely mean when she writes, "Hold off"?
options: Mr. Whitfield should wait before moving and rescanning the pallet.
The faucets should be held for a quality inspection.
The shipment should be returned to Hargrove Imports.
The backorders should be canceled.
questions.explanation: Mr. Whitfield가 팔레트에 새 태그를 붙여 배관 코너로 옮기겠다고 하자 'Hold off'라고 제지합니다. 수도꼭지가 애초에 입고 처리되지 않았다면 지금 스캔할 경우 오류가 나므로, 자신이 먼저 정정 기록을 만들 때까지 15분만 기다리라는 의미입니다.

questions.question: What will Mr. Whitfield most likely do next?
options: Contact Hargrove Imports about the mix-up
Search nearby bays and the returns cage for the tile pallet
Ship the faucet orders immediately
Replace the cracked wheel on a cart
questions.explanation: Mr. Whitfield가 진짜 타일 팔레트도 찾아볼지 묻자, Ms. Kovacs는 'Try bays 28 through 34 and the returns cage'라고 답합니다. 입고팀이 베이가 꽉 차면 반품 케이지에 초과 물량을 두기도 하므로, 그는 그 구역들을 수색할 것입니다.

passage:
Cole Barrett (8:40 A.M.): Anika, the city e-mailed—our drone permit for the bridge flyover covers Saturday only, sunrise to 10 A.M. Not the full weekend we requested.
Anika Joshi (8:42 A.M.): The shot list needs two passes at golden hour. One morning might do it if the wind cooperates.
Cole Barrett (8:44 A.M.): Saturday's forecast shows 8 km/h winds early, climbing after 9. The drone flies fine under 20, so the window is real—just thin.
Anika Joshi (8:46 A.M.): Then we treat Saturday like it's the only chance, because it is. Can you prep both batteries and the backup drone on Friday night?
Cole Barrett (8:48 A.M.): Already planned. One more thing: the permit requires a certified visual observer on-site. Russo did it last time, but he's on the Halverson shoot now.
Anika Joshi (8:50 A.M.): My old flight instructor, Dee Soto, keeps her observer card current. I'll call her this morning—she owes me a favor anyway.
Cole Barrett (8:52 A.M.): If she's in, send me her certificate number tonight—the city wants the observer's details filed 24 hours before the flight.
Anika Joshi (8:54 A.M.): You'll have it by 6. And Cole—charge the monitor van, too. Last time we nearly couldn't get the screens running.

questions.question: What problem does Mr. Barrett report?
options: The drone was damaged on a previous shoot.
A filming permit covers less time than was requested.
The bridge will be closed on Saturday.
The weather forecast predicts rain all weekend.
questions.explanation: 첫 메시지에서 시에서 발급한 드론 허가가 요청했던 주말 전체가 아니라 토요일 일출부터 오전 10시까지만 유효하다고 알립니다. 허가 시간이 요청보다 짧은 것이 문제입니다.

questions.question: At 8:46 A.M., what does Ms. Joshi most likely mean when she writes, "we treat Saturday like it's the only chance, because it is"?
options: The team must be fully prepared since there will be no second opportunity.
The shoot should be moved to Sunday if possible.
Saturday's footage will probably be unusable.
The city may cancel the permit at any time.
questions.explanation: 허가가 토요일 오전으로 한정되었고 바람도 9시 이후 강해질 예정이므로, 토요일을 유일한 기회로 여기고 완벽히 준비하자는 의미입니다. 그래서 곧바로 배터리 두 개와 예비 드론을 금요일 밤에 준비해 달라고 요청합니다.

questions.question: Why is Russo unable to serve as the visual observer?
options: His certification has expired.
He is working on a different production.
He is unavailable before 10 A.M.
He has moved to another city.
questions.explanation: Mr. Barrett은 지난번에는 Russo가 관측 요원을 맡았지만 지금은 Halverson 촬영에 투입되어 있다('he's on the Halverson shoot now')고 말합니다. 즉 다른 작품 일정 때문에 참여할 수 없는 것입니다.

questions.question: Why does Mr. Barrett need Ms. Soto's certificate number by tonight?
options: The rental company requires it for insurance.
Observer details must be filed with the city 24 hours before the flight.
Her certification expires tomorrow.
The production office closes early on Fridays.
questions.explanation: 8:52 A.M. 메시지에서 'the city wants the observer's details filed 24 hours before the flight'라고 명시합니다. 비행 24시간 전까지 관측 요원 정보를 시에 제출해야 하므로 오늘 밤까지 자격증 번호가 필요한 것입니다.

passage:
Raj Mehta (4:10 P.M.): Wendy, the main scoreboard is showing garbled characters on the away-team panel. The regional volleyball tournament starts at 9 A.M. Saturday.
Wendy Liu (4:12 P.M.): Did the reset from the control booth help? That fixed it during basketball season.
Raj Mehta (4:14 P.M.): Tried it twice. I suspect the data cable where it runs past the new air handler—the installers were drilling up there last week.
Wendy Liu (4:16 P.M.): ScoreTech's emergency line quotes a $450 call-out fee on top of repairs, and Friday is the soonest they would come.
Raj Mehta (4:18 P.M.): Friday is cutting it fine. If the cable is the culprit, I could splice in a temporary run myself tomorrow, and ScoreTech can do it properly later.
Wendy Liu (4:20 P.M.): I'd rather not void the service contract. Check the paperwork first—self-repairs may be excluded.
Raj Mehta (4:22 P.M.): Fair. Section 9 says minor cabling by certified staff is allowed, and my low-voltage certification is current.
Wendy Liu (4:24 P.M.): Then go ahead tomorrow, but book ScoreTech for Friday anyway as a safety net. If your fix holds, we'll downgrade their visit to a routine inspection and dodge the emergency fee.

questions.question: What does Mr. Mehta suspect caused the scoreboard problem?
options: A power outage during basketball season
A data cable damaged during recent installation work
Outdated scoreboard software

questions.explanation: Mr. Mehta는 새 공조 장치(air handler) 설치 기사들이 지난주에 그 위쪽에서 드릴 작업을 했다며, 그 근처를 지나는 데이터 케이블이 손상되었을 것으로 의심합니다('I suspect the data cable where it runs past the new air handler').

questions.question: At 4:18 P.M., what does Mr. Mehta most likely mean when he writes, "Friday is cutting it fine"?

questions.question: Why does Ms. Liu tell Mr. Mehta to check the paperwork?

To see whether self-repairs would void the service contract

questions.question: Why will ScoreTech still be booked for Friday?

To install a new air handler
To train Mr. Mehta on cabling
To inspect the away team's equipment
questions.explanation: Ms. Liu는 Mr. Mehta의 임시 수리를 승인하면서도 만약을 대비한 안전망('safety net')으로 금요일 ScoreTech 방문을 예약해 두라고 합니다. 임시 수리가 잘 유지되면 긴급 출동이 아닌 정기 점검으로 전환해 긴급 수수료를 피할 계획입니다.

passage:
Agnes Varga (2:05 P.M.): I found a silver watch under the bed in 714 during the checkout cleaning. It's engraved on the back: "To J.R. — 25 years."
Daniela Cruz (2:07 P.M.): Nice catch. Bag it, tag it with the room number and time, and bring it to my office. Don't leave it on the cart.
Milo Fischer (2:09 P.M.): 714 checked out at 11—a Mr. Jonas Reinholt, flying out of Gate City this evening according to his profile. Want me to call him?

questions.question: At 2:23 P.M., what does Mr. Fischer most likely mean when he writes, "he's still in the city and nearly cried"?

passage: SAN MATEO (June 2) — Nimbra Technologies, a logistics startup founded just three years ago, announced on Monday that it has raised $40 million in Series B funding led by Crestpoint Ventures. [1] The company's software uses artificial intelligence to plan delivery routes for small and midsized retailers, cutting fuel costs by an average of 18 percent. [2] Nimbra currently serves about 600 clients across North America and plans to use the new capital to enter European markets early next year. [3] The company will also double its engineering staff, adding roughly 80 positions at its San Mateo headquarters and at a new office in Toronto. [4] Chief Executive Officer Dana Whitfield said the funding round was completed in just six weeks, which she described as a sign of strong investor confidence in the logistics software sector. Industry analysts expect demand for route-optimization tools to continue growing as fuel prices remain high and retailers look for ways to keep delivery promises without raising prices.

questions.question: What is the main purpose of the article?
options: To review a new software product for consumers
To report on a company's recent investment funding
To announce the merger of two logistics firms
To explain why fuel prices have increased
questions.explanation: 기사 첫 문장에서 Nimbra Technologies가 Crestpoint Ventures 주도로 4천만 달러 규모의 시리즈 B 투자를 유치했다고 발표한 내용을 전하고 있습니다. 기사 전체가 이 투자 유치와 자금의 활용 계획을 다루고 있으므로 (B)가 정답입니다. 합병(merger)이나 소비자용 제품 리뷰에 대한 내용은 없습니다.

options: Acquire a competing startup
Lower its software subscription fees
Expand into markets in Europe

questions.explanation: 지문 중반에 'plans to use the new capital to enter European markets early next year'라고 명시되어 있어, 새 자금으로 내년 초 유럽 시장에 진출할 계획임을 알 수 있습니다. 경쟁사 인수, 요금 인하, 자체 배송 차량 도입에 대한 언급은 없으므로 (C)가 정답입니다.

questions.question: In which of the positions marked [1], [2], [3], and [4] does the following sentence best belong? "Several clients have reported even larger savings during peak holiday periods."
questions.explanation: 삽입 문장은 '일부 고객들은 성수기에 훨씬 더 큰 절감 효과를 보고했다'는 내용으로, 'even larger savings'는 앞에 절감(savings)에 대한 언급이 있어야 자연스럽습니다. [2] 바로 앞 문장에서 연료비를 평균 18% 절감한다고 했으므로, 그 절감 효과를 보충 설명하는 위치인 [2]가 정답입니다.

questions.question: What is suggested about the Series B funding round?
options: It was finalized relatively quickly.
It was smaller than the company expected.

questions.explanation: CEO Dana Whitfield가 'the funding round was completed in just six weeks'라고 말하며 이를 투자자 신뢰의 신호로 표현했습니다. 즉, 투자 라운드가 단 6주 만에 비교적 빠르게 마무리되었음을 시사하므로 (A)가 정답입니다. 시리즈 B는 첫 외부 투자가 아니며, 주도 투자사가 유럽 회사라는 언급도 없습니다.

passage:
From Checkout Lines to Cooking Classes: Retail Reinvents Itself

Walk into Hartwell & Finch, a department store in downtown Avondale, and you may find a pottery workshop in the homewares section or a wine-tasting event near the food hall. Stores that once relied solely on merchandise sales are increasingly using in-store experiences to draw customers who might otherwise shop online. According to a recent survey by the Avondale Retail Council, 64 percent of shoppers under 40 said they were more likely to visit a store that offered classes, demonstrations, or live events. Retail consultant Priya Raman says the strategy works because experiences cannot be downloaded or delivered. "A scarf can be bought anywhere," she explained, "but an afternoon learning to knit one is memorable." The shift requires investment, however. Hartwell & Finch spent nearly $2 million converting its third floor into an event space, and it now employs four full-time event coordinators. Store director Malcolm Reyes says the spending has paid off: foot traffic has risen 22 percent since the renovation, and sales in adjacent departments have grown as well.

questions.question: What is the article mainly about?
options: A trend of stores offering activities to attract shoppers
The closure of traditional department stores
A rise in online shopping among older consumers
New government regulations affecting retailers
questions.explanation: 기사 전체가 매장 내에서 공방, 시음회, 강좌 같은 체험을 제공하여 고객을 끌어들이는 '체험형 소매(experiential retail)' 트렌드를 다루고 있습니다. 매장 폐업, 고령층의 온라인 쇼핑, 정부 규제는 언급되지 않으므로 (A)가 정답입니다.

questions.question: The word "draw" in paragraph 1 is closest in meaning to
options: sketch
attract
select
remove

options: It opened a second location in Avondale.
It reduced the size of its food hall.

It began selling products online for the first time.
questions.explanation: 지문 후반에 'Hartwell & Finch spent nearly $2 million converting its third floor into an event space'라고 하여, 3층을 이벤트 공간으로 개조하는 데 약 200만 달러를 들였다고 명시되어 있습니다. 따라서 (C)가 정답입니다. 2호점 개점이나 온라인 판매 개시에 대한 언급은 없습니다.

questions.question: According to Mr. Reyes, what has happened since the renovation?

More customers have been visiting the store.

The store has extended its opening hours.
questions.explanation: 마지막 문장에서 매장 책임자 Malcolm Reyes는 'foot traffic has risen 22 percent since the renovation'이라고 말합니다. foot traffic(방문객 수)이 22% 증가했다는 것은 더 많은 고객이 매장을 방문하고 있다는 뜻이므로 (B)가 정답입니다.

passage:
Eastline Extension to Open Ahead of Schedule

GRANVILLE (March 14) — The Granville Transit Authority (GTA) confirmed yesterday that the long-awaited Eastline light rail extension will open on May 3, nearly two months ahead of schedule. The 9-kilometer extension adds five stations and connects the Riverside business district with the university campus and the regional hospital. Trains will run every six minutes during peak hours and every twelve minutes at other times. GTA spokesperson Olivia Tran credited the early completion to mild winter weather and a decision to prefabricate track sections off-site, which reduced construction time by several months. The project, budgeted at $310 million, came in roughly $12 million under its original estimate. To mark the opening, the GTA will offer free rides on the entire Eastline during the first weekend of service. City officials predict the extension will remove up to 4,000 cars from downtown roads each weekday. Local business owners along the route, who endured two years of construction detours, say they are hopeful the new stations will bring back customers who had been avoiding the area.

questions.question: What is the purpose of the article?
options: To explain delays in a construction project
To announce the early opening of a rail line extension
To criticize a transit authority's spending
To describe a plan to widen downtown roads
questions.explanation: 기사 첫 문장에서 Eastline 경전철 연장 구간이 예정보다 약 두 달 빨리 5월 3일에 개통된다고 발표한 내용을 전하고 있습니다. 공사 지연이 아니라 조기 개통 소식이므로 (B)가 정답입니다. 예산도 초과가 아닌 절감으로 보도되어 (C)는 오답입니다.

options: operate
compete
escape
manage

questions.question: According to Ms. Tran, what helped the project finish early?
options: Hiring additional construction crews
Reducing the number of planned stations

Receiving extra funding from the city
questions.explanation: GTA 대변인 Olivia Tran은 조기 완공의 요인으로 온화한 겨울 날씨와 'a decision to prefabricate track sections off-site', 즉 선로 구간을 현장 밖에서 사전 제작한 결정을 꼽았습니다. 이로 인해 공사 기간이 수개월 단축되었다고 했으므로 (C)가 정답입니다.

questions.question: What is indicated about business owners along the route?
options: They opposed the construction of the extension.
They experienced disruptions during construction.

They plan to relocate closer to the university.
questions.explanation: 마지막 문장에서 노선 주변 상인들이 'endured two years of construction detours', 즉 2년간의 공사 우회로 인한 불편을 겪었다고 언급됩니다. 이는 공사 기간 동안 영업에 지장이 있었음을 나타내므로 (B)가 정답입니다. 상인들은 공사에 반대했다기보다 새 역이 손님을 다시 데려오길 기대하고 있습니다.

passage:
Suburban Office Market Shows Signs of Recovery, Report Finds

The quarterly market report released Tuesday by Calloway Property Research paints a mixed picture of the Brackenford metropolitan area's commercial real estate sector. [1] Downtown office vacancy remained high at 21 percent, virtually unchanged from the previous quarter. [2] In contrast, suburban office parks recorded their strongest quarter in five years, with vacancy falling to 11 percent as companies sought smaller, more flexible spaces closer to where employees live. [3] Average asking rents in the suburbs rose 4.2 percent year over year, while downtown rents declined slightly. [4] The report attributes the shift to the continued popularity of hybrid work arrangements, which have reduced demand for large central headquarters. Lead analyst Marcus Obi cautioned, however, that downtown properties with modern amenities are still leasing well. "Buildings with fitness centers, upgraded ventilation, and conference facilities are outperforming the market," he noted. "It is the older, unrenovated towers that are struggling to find tenants." Calloway forecasts that overall vacancy will begin to decline by the middle of next year.

questions.question: What is the main topic of the article?
options: Trends in a region's office rental market
The construction of a new suburban office park
A rise in residential housing prices
A proposal to renovate downtown towers
questions.explanation: 기사는 Calloway Property Research의 분기 보고서를 인용하여 Brackenford 대도시권의 도심 및 교외 사무실 공실률과 임대료 동향을 분석하고 있습니다. 즉, 지역 사무실 임대 시장의 동향이 주제이므로 (A)가 정답입니다. 주거용 부동산이나 특정 건설 사업은 다루지 않습니다.

questions.question: According to the report, why have suburban offices become more popular?
options: Suburban rents have fallen significantly.
Hybrid work has changed companies' space needs.
New highways have improved suburban access.
Downtown parking fees have increased.
questions.explanation: 보고서는 이러한 변화를 'the continued popularity of hybrid work arrangements' 때문이라고 분석합니다. 하이브리드 근무로 대형 도심 본사에 대한 수요가 줄고, 기업들이 직원 거주지와 가까운 작고 유연한 공간을 찾게 되었다는 것이므로 (B)가 정답입니다. 교외 임대료는 오히려 4.2% 상승했습니다.

questions.question: In which of the positions marked [1], [2], [3], and [4] does the following sentence best belong? "Several large firms there have given up entire floors as their leases expired."
questions.explanation: 삽입 문장의 'there'는 특정 장소를 가리켜야 하며, 대형 회사들이 층 전체를 포기했다는 내용은 도심의 높은 공실률을 보충 설명합니다. [2] 바로 앞 문장이 도심 공실률이 21%로 높다는 내용이므로, 그 원인을 구체적으로 설명하는 [2]가 가장 자연스럽습니다.

questions.question: What does Mr. Obi indicate about downtown buildings?
options: They will all be converted into apartments.
Those with modern features are still attracting tenants.
They are no longer profitable for any owners.
Their rents are rising faster than suburban rents.
questions.explanation: 수석 애널리스트 Marcus Obi는 피트니스 센터, 개선된 환기 시설, 회의 시설을 갖춘 건물들은 시장 평균을 상회하는 성과를 내고 있으며, 임차인을 구하기 어려운 것은 오래되고 개보수되지 않은 건물들이라고 말합니다. 즉, 현대적 설비를 갖춘 도심 건물은 여전히 임차인을 끌어들이고 있으므로 (B)가 정답입니다.

passage:
The Quiet Builder: A Profile of Renata Solis

When Renata Solis founded GreenShell Packaging twelve years ago, she worked out of a rented garage with two employees and a single molding machine. Today, the company she leads produces compostable food containers for more than 2,000 restaurants and grocery chains, and it employs over 400 people at plants in Davenport and Kingsbury. Solis, who trained as a chemical engineer, spent her early career at a large plastics manufacturer, where she grew frustrated by the industry's slow response to environmental concerns. She left to develop a plant-fiber container that could break down in a home compost bin within eight weeks. The first two years were difficult; a modest loan from a regional development fund kept the company afloat while Solis refined her manufacturing process. Her persistence paid off when a national salad chain placed an order for five million containers. Despite GreenShell's growth, Solis still reviews product samples herself every Friday morning. "The day I stop checking the details," she says, "is the day we become ordinary." She is currently writing a book about sustainable manufacturing, due out next spring.

questions.question: What is the purpose of the article?
options: To describe the career of a company founder
To advertise a new line of food containers
To report on a factory closure in Davenport
To compare two packaging manufacturers
questions.explanation: 이 기사는 GreenShell Packaging의 창업자 Renata Solis의 창업 배경, 초기 어려움, 성공 과정과 경영 철학을 소개하는 인물 프로필 기사입니다. 따라서 창업자의 경력을 소개하는 것이 목적이므로 (A)가 정답입니다.

questions.question: Why did Ms. Solis leave her previous employer?
options: She was offered a teaching position.
She was dissatisfied with the industry's environmental record.
She wanted to move closer to her family.
Her division was eliminated in a restructuring.
questions.explanation: 지문에서 Solis는 대형 플라스틱 제조업체에서 일하던 중 'grew frustrated by the industry's slow response to environmental concerns', 즉 업계가 환경 문제에 더디게 대응하는 것에 좌절감을 느껴 퇴사했다고 설명합니다. 따라서 (B)가 정답입니다.

questions.question: The word "modest" in paragraph 1 is closest in meaning to
options: humble in manner
relatively small
extremely risky
well publicized
questions.explanation: 'a modest loan from a regional development fund'에서 modest는 대출의 규모가 '크지 않은, 소박한'이라는 의미로 쓰였습니다. 따라서 relatively small(비교적 작은)이 가장 가깝습니다. humble in manner(겸손한)는 사람의 태도를 나타낼 때의 의미이므로 이 문맥에는 맞지 않습니다.

questions.question: What is mentioned about Ms. Solis's current activities?
options: She inspects product samples weekly.
She teaches chemical engineering part-time.

Rental Market Cools After Two Years of Record Growth

Apartment hunters in the Sarsfield metropolitan area are finally getting some relief. Foundry District Becomes a Magnet for Young Companies

Three years ago, the old Foundry District on Halverton's east side was best known for its empty warehouses. Of the 62 companies that have finished the program, 51 are still operating, and together they employ more than 900 people. Graduates include Saffron Analytics, a data firm that recently signed a lease for an entire warehouse floor, and Pellucid Health, which makes scheduling software for medical clinics. Collective director Amara Diallo says the program's strength is its selectivity; fewer than one in ten applicants is accepted, and preference goes to founders who already have a working product and at least one paying customer. The storefront at 12 Cordova Lane has held a candle maker, a vintage clothing seller, and a hot sauce brand—all within the past year. Harbor Ferries to Get First Major Upgrade in Twenty Years

MORELAND BAY (Feb. 9) — The Moreland Bay Ferry Service will modernize its aging fleet and terminals under a $95 million plan approved by the regional transit board last week. The service, which carries about 18,000 passengers daily between five waterfront communities and the city center, has operated essentially unchanged since 2006, and several of its vessels are approaching the end of their service lives. Under the plan, four new hybrid-electric ferries will replace the six oldest diesel boats beginning in 2028. Although the new vessels are fewer in number, each carries nearly twice as many passengers, allowing the service to increase total capacity while cutting fuel consumption by an estimated 40 percent. Terminal improvements will include covered waiting areas, real-time arrival displays, and ramps that adjust automatically to tide levels, which will speed up boarding for passengers with bicycles, strollers, and wheelchairs. Commuter advocacy group Bay Riders United praised the investment but urged the board to also extend evening service hours, noting that the last ferry currently departs at 8:40 P.M. Board chair Vincent Osei said a study of expanded hours will be completed by the end of the year.

passage:
Building on Patience: Theodore Lam's Long Game

In an industry known for quick profits, commercial developer Theodore Lam has built his reputation on waiting. The founder of Lamwood Properties, now one of the region's most respected development firms, is famous for holding sites for years until the surrounding neighborhood matures. His best-known project, the Calloway Mills complex, illustrates the approach. Lam acquired the abandoned textile factory in 2014, when the riverfront district had little foot traffic and most investors avoided the area. Rather than building immediately, he spent five years leasing portions of the property at low rates to artists and small workshops, which gradually drew visitors to the district. Only then did Lamwood begin its full renovation, converting the mills into a mix of offices, shops, and apartments that is now fully leased with a waiting list. "Everyone wants to be the last investor into a neighborhood," Lam said in a rare interview. "I would rather be the first, and then be patient." Lam, who grew up above his parents' hardware store, says the experience taught him that districts thrive when small businesses can afford to stay. Accordingly, every Lamwood project reserves 15 percent of its commercial space for local independent businesses at below-market rents.

COLEFAX (May 28) — Energy storage startup Verdant Grid announced Thursday that it has raised $75 million to expand its network of neighborhood battery stations, which store surplus solar power during the day and release it to the local grid in the evening. Founder and CEO Elias Toro, a former utility engineer, said the company will also begin testing larger stations near two retired power plants, where existing transmission lines can carry far more electricity.
